transcript:
Date: 2025-11-12
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (CSM), Alex Romero (SE); Maya Lopez (Head of ML), Tom Reed (Infra Lead), Sana Patel (VP Product), Jules Martin (SRE)

[00:00] Jordan Kim: Hi everyone, thanks for joining the QBR. Quick check — is this still 15:00 UTC for you folks?
[00:08] Maya Lopez: Yeah that's correct, thanks Jordan.
[00:12] Jordan Kim: Great. We'll run ~45 mins. Agenda: usage and cost trends, reliability incidents, roadmap items, and then next steps. Priya and Alex are with me.
[00:25] Priya Desai: Hi all, we'll also cover the security pack requests at the end.
[00:30] Tom Reed: Sounds good. Quick note, Jules is on for SRE questions.
[00:34] Jordan Kim: Perfect. Maya, can you give a quick update on how your teams are using Redwood since our last check-in?
[00:42] Maya Lopez: Sure — so overall we're up about 2.6x token volume vs last quarter. The bulk of growth is prod chat flows and an increase in background embeddings. Cost per month has crept up; we saw a spike mid-Oct when we rolled out the new recommendation prompt.
[00:58] Alex Romero: When you say spike, was that latency-related or just token volume?
[01:03] Maya Lopez: Mostly token volume and a few long running responses which also hit higher seq lengths — about 1% of calls were hitting 8k+ tokens.
[01:12] Jordan Kim: Got it. That explains both cost and the occasional latency outliers. Tom, from infra — any notes on the reliability incidents?
[01:20] Tom Reed: We saw three incidents flagged as P1-ish — two were region failovers and one was a slow KV cache miss that cascaded. Latency spikes were transient but we want better tail latency.
[01:32] Jules Martin: The slow KV cache miss — the cache write seemed to have GC pressure in the customer's side, not sure if the calls were batched. The metrics show higher p99 at 800ms during that window.
[01:44] Alex Romero: We can run a targeted benchmark to reproduce that with your traffic shape — our KV/prefix caching can reduce those misses significantly if configured.
[01:52] Maya Lopez: That'd be helpful. Also curious about Dedicated — would that reduce the tail latency for us?
[01:58] Jordan Kim: Yes, Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools which reduce noisy neighbor risk and give more predictable throughput/latency. For your qps profile, a small Dedicated cluster plus autoscale could reduce p99 by 30-50% in our experience for similar customers.
[02:12] Sana Patel: What's the cost delta we should expect between hosted usage vs reserved Dedicated? We need to justify to finance.
[02:20] Jordan Kim: Good question. It depends on utilization. For heavy sustained throughput, Dedicated monthly commit often lowers unit cost by ~20-40% relative to pure hosted on pay-as-you-go. We'll send a committed capacity vs on-demand comparison with your numbers after this call.
[02:35] Maya Lopez: Please include the burst/overage pricing — we need to see worst-case.
[02:39] Jordan Kim: Absolutely.
[02:41] Priya Desai: On the security side — you requested SOC2, SAML integration, and audit logs last quarter; we've prepared the SOC2 summary and an architecture diagram for VPC/private.
[02:52] Maya Lopez: For data residency we need VPC peering or the private deployment. We have customers in EU; we need guarantees around regional data processing.
[03:02] Jordan Kim: For data residency, Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) is the path. It provides customer-managed networking and KMS integrations. For many EU use cases we do regionally isolated Private installs. We'll share the network diagram.
[03:13] Tom Reed: Also need details on key management — does Private support HSM-backed KMS?
[03:18] Alex Romero: Yes, Private supports customer KMS and HSM integrations; we'll include the KMS integration notes.
[03:24] Maya Lopez: Great. Back to reliability — can we get a short term mitigation for the KV cache misses while we plan a Dedicated pilot?
[03:32] Alex Romero: Sure — immediate fixes: adjust batch windowing, enable persistent KV cache with larger cache retention, and enable more aggressive prefix caching for your high-frequency flows. I can run a config proposal and benchmark.
[03:44] Jules Martin: That config change — will it affect cost materially?
[03:48] Alex Romero: Minimal — slightly higher memory use but you'd save tokens by avoiding re-computation, so usually net cost down. There may be a small infra delta if you provision more memory.
[03:58] Sana Patel: On the roadmap, we have an internal goal to lower average latency by 20% for Q1. If Dedicated plus these cache changes get us there, we can prioritize the pilot.
[04:09] Jordan Kim: Understood. We recommend a two-week pilot on Dedicated with a benchmark harness: the goal is to validate p50/p95/p99 improvements and cost delta.
[04:18] Maya Lopez: Two-week pilot sounds reasonable. We'll need a clear success criteria doc.
[04:22] Priya Desai: We'll draft an SLO and success criteria checklist: target p50 < 120ms, p95 < 350ms, p99 < 700ms for your sampled workload. Is that aligned?
[04:33] Tom Reed: Those look reasonable as targets. We'll confirm after we provide traffic CSV.
[04:38] Jordan Kim: Great — Alex will run the initial config test. Alex, can you outline the benchmark steps?
[04:45] Alex Romero: Yeah — step 1: ingest representative prompts and traffic profile from Maya; step 2: run baseline on hosted as-is; step 3: run Dedicated small cluster with proposed cache settings; step 4: compare token cost, latency histograms, and tail behavior. I'll include a spreadsheet with cost math.
[05:05] Maya Lopez: Please add a column for model determinism and output quality — we had a slight regress when we applied a quantization profile in staging.
[05:13] Alex Romero: Good point — we'll include a quality-check set (exact-match and human-sample checks).
[05:18] Jordan Kim: On pricing — finance will want committed discount levels, early termination terms. I'll attach the standard reserved capacity T&Cs but we can surface custom terms for enterprise.
[05:29] Sana Patel: Also need to ensure SSO via SAML with our IdP and RBAC mapping for teams.
[05:35] Priya Desai: We support SAML SSO and RBAC mapping; we'll send the SAML metadata and a mapping example.
[05:42] Tom Reed: For auditability, we need token-level tracing and per-route logs retained for 90 days. Is that possible?
[05:48] Alex Romero: Yes — Redwood Console supports token-level cost/latency breakdowns and we can configure longer retention as an add-on. We'll include retention options and pricing.
[05:58] Maya Lopez: One more thing — do you have an example of how fallback policies are configured if a region has a partial outage? We need automatic graceful degradation.
[06:08] Jordan Kim: Yes, smart routing policies support region fallback and model variant fallback. We'll share a sample config (json/yaml) — note that our generated sample might have some vendor names a bit off in the transcript export — but the doc will be clean.
[06:21] Jules Martin: Who's the technical owner on Redwood side for the benchmark?
[06:24] Jordan Kim: Alex will lead the technical bench; Priya will coordinate resources and security artifacts.
[06:29] Alex Romero: I'll propose a 60-minute bench run and then a 2-week Dedicated pilot.
[06:34] Sana Patel: Timeline wise we want pilot results before our Jan planning week.
[06:38] Jordan Kim: We can aim to deliver bench results by end of November and start pilot in early December.
[06:44] Maya Lopez: That works.
[06:46] Jordan Kim: Ok recap of next steps — I'll send pricing and the usage dashboard, Priya will send SOC2 and SAML metadata, Alex will schedule the benchmark and share config, Maya will provide prompt sets/traffic profile. Any blockers?
[06:59] Tom Reed: No blockers on our side; just need the benchmark timeslot.
[07:02] Maya Lopez: We'll get the CSV by Wednesday.
[07:05] Jordan Kim: Great. Anything else before we close?
[07:09] Sana Patel: One ask — can you include model quantization recommendations? We saw the staging regression.
[07:15] Alex Romero: Yes, Redwood Optimize has quant profiles; I'll include model and quant suggestions and the expected cost/quality tradeoffs.
[07:23] Jordan Kim: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the docs and schedule.
[07:27] Maya Lopez: Thanks, talk soon.
[07:29] Jordan Kim: Bye.

Notes: occasional transcription artifacts — e.g., "Sam'l" instead of SAML, "K V cache" spaced — original audio had slight overlaps. Shared artifacts referenced: usage dashboard (internal link), SOC2_summary.pdf (link), dedicated-pilot-plan.xlsx (link), kv-benchmark-results-template.csv (link).
